$comment: Source of truth for the People Data Labs migration guides. Tables in docs/migrate-from-people-data-labs*.mdx are generated from this file: edit it, then run npm run sync:migrations. npm run check:migrations verifies every CompanyEnrich path and filter against openapi/v2.json.

fidelity.same: Same field name, meaning, and values.
fidelity.renamed: Same meaning under a different name or path.
fidelity.transformed: Same information in a different shape, format, or casing. Convert it in code.
fidelity.lossy: Related information with a different definition, scale, or granularity. Review before you rely on it.

endpoints.note: Send the host only, such as `stripe.com`. PDL keeps paths for hosted sites such as `etsy.com/shop`; those have no domain to send.
Every property you send must match. When several companies match, the highest-ranked one is returned, with no likelihood score. No match returns `404` and is not charged.
No equivalent inputs. Resolve a domain first, for example from the `website` in records you already stored.
Up to 50 domains per request, against 100 parameter objects in PDL. Domains only. Items come back in request order with a `status` of `found`, `not-found`, `invalid-domain`, or `pending`.
Background job for up to 10,000 domains. Poll the batch, then download JSON, NDJSON, or CSV. See [Bulk jobs and exports](/docs/bulk-jobs-and-exports).
Rewrite each query as a `filter` object. See [Translate search queries](/docs/migrate-from-people-data-labs-search).
Search responses carry no total. Send the same filter to the count endpoint, which is free.
Work emails only. The API resolves the company from the email domain, then matches the person by common address patterns. The person is the response body; PDL nests it under `data`.
No equivalent. `name` here means a name with a company, school, or location. People search by `query` and `domain` returns candidates without a confidence score.
No bulk person enrichment in V2. Call `POST /v2/people/enrich` per work email within your rate limit.
Rewrite each query as a `filter` object, plus a `company` query for employer attributes. The `dataset` parameter has no equivalent.
No ranked identity candidates. People search returns matches without a score.
Takes a CompanyEnrich person ID. PDL IDs do not carry over.
A separate call that returns `status`, `email`, and `certainty`. Costs 10 credits only when it finds an email your account has not accessed before.
Free. For `field=title`, `industry`, `country`, or `region`, use position autocomplete, the industry list, or the geo endpoints. There is no school, major, or skill lookup.
No name or URL cleaner. Company autocomplete suggests domains for a partial name.
No address parser. The free geo endpoints find country, state, and city IDs by name.
No equivalent.
No IP-to-company lookup.
No title classifier. Position autocomplete suggests titles.
No job posting data in V2. Workforce history is headcount, not postings.
No change feed. Every record has an `updatedAt` timestamp.
No sandbox. Test with mocked HTTP and the free endpoints: `GET /v2/me`, counts, and lookups.

companySize.title: Company size
companySize.note: The labels translate one to one. The meaning depends on the field: PDL `size` is self-reported, so search it with `reportedEmployees`; CompanyEnrich `employees` is calculated.

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.note: The ranges have different boundaries. When a PDL range spans two CompanyEnrich ranges, a search on both returns a wider set.

seniority.title: Seniority
seniority.note: PDL returns an array of levels; CompanyEnrich returns one. CompanyEnrich also has `founder`, `head`, and `intern`.

rows.note: Not mapped automatically. `intern` and `entry` both overlap.

department.title: Job role and department
department.note: Only roles with a clear counterpart are mapped. For the rest, filter on `position` phrases instead.

fundingRound.title: Funding round
fundingRound.note: These are search filter values. Company records return labels such as `Series A` instead.

rows.note: No exact value. CompanyEnrich also has `venture` and `other`.
